BASE-ACCESS-002.summary: Otherwise-admissible protected API requests return 401 at session validation, while native documents and generated RPC preserve their identifiable session-denial protocols with no private product payload or requested mutation. Sign-out pauses coordinated private API GETs and drains admitted reads before revocation; a bounded drain failure reports an error and resumes reads for retry. Independent server admission remains required.
BASE-ACCESS-002.was: A session expires after at most 30 days of inactivity; sign-out revokes that session. Every operator endpoint requires a valid session and returns 401 without one.
BASE-ACCESS-002.now: A session expires after at most 30 days of inactivity; sign-out revokes that session. A valid session is required before an operator request reads private product data or performs its requested action. A protected operator document and each private generated server-function handler validate the session independently; a document gate does not authorize a function call. For an otherwise-admissible request that reaches session validation, a protected operator HTTP API returns 401 when the session is missing, expired, or revoked; a protected document returns its native sign-in response; and a generated transport may encode an identifiable session denial or sign-in redirect in its framework protocol, including a 200 serialized redirect. No such denial response exposes private product data or performs the requested mutation. Declared public exceptions remain governed by BASE-ACCESS-003, and host, method, Origin/CSRF, input, and runtime guards retain their normal order.

REL-006.summary: Expose parent authoring from issue details and root/child browsing filters while retaining workspace boundaries, cycle refusal, version checks and existing child detachment behavior.
REL-006.was: An issue has at most one parent. Vector rejects self-parenting and ancestry cycles; changing a parent never changes status, team, project, cycle, or assignee, and deleting a parent makes each direct child a root issue.
REL-006.now: An issue has at most one parent. An operator can set, replace, or clear it from issue details. Vector rejects self-parenting and ancestry cycles; changing a parent never changes status, team, project, cycle, or assignee, and deleting a parent makes each direct child a root issue. SEARCH-002.summary: Exact primary identifiers rank first alongside bounded full-text issue/project/accessible-view results; failed index reads retain only a newly admitted primary result. Forward migration 0018 stores stable source TEXT IDs in FTS and joins by ID, preserving identity across source rowid changes and index rebuilds.
SEARCH-002.was: An exact issue identifier lookup reads the primary record and returns it even while full-text indexing is delayed or failed.
SEARCH-002.now: An exact issue identifier lookup reads the primary record and returns it even while full-text indexing is delayed or unavailable, subject to the archive choice in SEARCH-001. On a successful full-text read, that exact issue ranks first, without duplicating it or dropping other matching issues, projects or accessible saved views; results remain bounded. Primary identity, archive choice and operator/session/workspace admission are rechecked before returning results, including after an index failure.

SEARCH-003.summary: Source-transaction triggers retain immediate atomic indexing while migration 0018 replaces rowid mappings with stable source TEXT IDs. FTS read failure retains the admitted exact primary exception under SEARCH-002; other failures remain visibly unavailable.
SEARCH-003.was: Created or changed searchable text appears in full-text results within 10 seconds. A failed indexing job is visible to operators with its last successful index time; Vector never presents known-stale results as complete.
SEARCH-003.now: Created or changed searchable text appears in full-text results within 10 seconds. Database triggers maintain the full-text entries in the same transaction as searchable source changes, so a committed source change cannot leave its corresponding entry behind. If an index query fails, the exact primary-record lookup remains available under SEARCH-002; other searches are reported unavailable with the last successful index time; Vector never presents a known index failure as a complete empty result.
